'''Matthew Martin Little''' (born November 24, 1984) is an American attorney and politician and a former member of the [[Minnesota Senate]]. A member of the [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party]] (DFL), he represented District 58 in the southern [[Twin Cities]] metropolitan area from 2017 to 2021.<ref name="lrl">{{cite web |title=Little, Matt - Legislator Record |url=https://www.lrl.mn.gov/legdb/fulldetail?id=15490 |website=Minnesota Legislators Past & Present |publisher=[[Minnesota Legislative Reference Library]] |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> Little is the DFL nominee for the [[United States House of Representatives]] in [[Minnesota's 2nd congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Minnesota#District 2|2026]]. He received the party endorsement for the seat in May 2026 and won the DFL primary on August 11.<ref name="cd2-dflconvention">{{cite news |last=Kashiwagi |first=Sydney |title=Former Lakeville Mayor Matt Little wins DFL endorsement for Rep. Angie Craig's seat |url=https://www.startribune.com/second-district-democrats-weigh-endorsement-to-replace-rep-angie-craig/601836410 |access-date=August 11, 2026 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune]] |date=May 9, 2026}}</ref><ref name="CBS-endorsement">{{cite news |last=Wight |first=Conor |title=Matt Little wins DFL party endorsement for Minnesota's 2nd Congressional District |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/matt-little-dfl-party-endorsement-2nd-congressional-district/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |work=[[WCCO-TV|CBS Minnesota]] |date=May 10, 2026}}</ref><ref name="FOXPrimaryWin">{{cite news |last=Fitzgerald |first=Kilat |title=Minnesota 2nd Congressional District primary election: Matt Little wins DFL nomination |url=https://www.fox9.com/news/minnesota-primary-election-results-cd-2-2026 |work=[[KMSP-TV|FOX 9]] |date=August 11, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

== Biography ==

=== Early life and education ===
Matt Little was born and raised in [[Lakeville, Minnesota]], graduating from [[Rosemount High School]] in 2003 before earning a bachelor's degree in [[political science]] from the [[University of Minnesota Morris]] in 2007.<ref name="RiverTowns2015">{{cite news |last=Hansen |first=Nathan |title=Lakeville mayor Little will run for Senate in District 58 |url=https://www.rivertowns.net/news/government-and-politics/3846230-lakeville-mayor-little-will-run-senate-district-58 |date=September 24, 2015 |work=RiverTowns |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="stw_20161029">{{cite news |title=Senate District 58 candidate questionnaire 2016 |url=http://sunthisweek.com/2016/10/29/203348/ |access-date=December 17, 2016 |work=Sun Thisweek |publisher=ECM Publishers |date=October 29, 2016}}</ref><ref name="lrl" />

Little worked as a [[Union representative|regional field coordinator]] for the [[National Association of Letter Carriers]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], for two years and spent a year teaching English in [[Chile]] before attending the [[University of Minnesota Law School]].<ref name="rtp_20150924">{{cite news |last=Hansen |first=Nathan |title=Rosemount grad Little will run for Senate seat |url=http://www.rosemounttownpages.com/news/politics/3846298-rosemount-grad-little-will-run-senate-seat |access-date=December 17, 2016 |work=Rosemount Town Pages |publisher=[[Forum Communications]] |date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021004309/http://www.rosemounttownpages.com/news/politics/3846298-rosemount-grad-little-will-run-senate-seat |archive-date=October 21, 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="RiverTowns2015" /> In 2014, he earned his [[Juris Doctor]], graduating ''[[Latin honors|magna cum laude]]''.<ref name="lrl" /><ref name="stw_20161029" /><ref name="Hastings2022">{{cite news |title=Former Sen. Matt Little announces run for Dakota County Attorney |url=https://www.hastingsjournal.news/stories/former-sen-matt-little-announces-run-for-dakota-county-attorney%2C22403 |work=Hastings Journal |date=January 24, 2022 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

=== Early political career and attorney practice ===
In 2010, Little was elected to the [[Lakeville, Minnesota|Lakeville]] City Council. In 2012, at age 27, he became the youngest person to be elected mayor of Lakeville.<ref name="RiverTowns2015" /><ref name="lrl" /><ref name="StribYoungest">{{cite news |last=Adams |first=Jim |title=At 27, mayor is Lakeville's youngest |url=https://www.startribune.com/at-27-mayor-is-lakeville-s-youngest/178479971 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune|Star Tribune]] |date=November 10, 2012 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Strib-launch">{{cite news |last=Kashiwagi |first=Sydney |title=Matt Little, former state senator and Lakeville mayor, enters race to replace Rep. Angie Craig |url=https://www.startribune.com/former-state-sen-and-lakeville-mayor-matt-little-enters-race-to-replace-rep-angie-craig/601341721 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune]] |date=April 30, 2025 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> He served as mayor until 2016, when he was elected to the state Senate.<ref name="lrl" /><ref name="Strib-launch" />

Little works as an attorney at his Lakeville firm, Little Law, which focuses on [[medical malpractice]] and [[personal injury law]].<ref name="rtp_20150924" /><ref name="LittleLaw">{{cite web |title=Practice Areas |url=https://alittlelawfirm.com/practice-areas/ |publisher=Little Law, LLC |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> The ''Minnesota Star Tribune'' reported in 2025 that his practice represented seniors and people with disabilities as well as people who had been injured through negligence or abuse.<ref name="Strib-launch" />

=== Minnesota Senate ===
[[File:Senator Matt Little presides over the Committee on Banned Bills.jpg|thumb|left|Little (center) in 2019]]

In [[2016 Minnesota Senate election|2016]], Little was narrowly elected to the [[Minnesota Senate]], defeating Republican Tim Pitcher by 387 votes.<ref name="SOS2016">{{cite web |title=Results for State Senator District 58 |url=https://electionresults.sos.mn.gov/results/Index?ErsElectionId=100&scenario=StateSenate&DistrictId=546&show=Go |publisher=[[Minnesota Secretary of State]] |date=November 23, 2016 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="lrl" /> He served on the Jobs and Economic Growth Finance and Policy, Transportation Finance and Policy, and Veterans and Military Affairs Finance and Policy committees.<ref name="lrl" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.senate.mn/members/member_bio.php?member_id=1237 |title=Senator Matt Little |website=Minnesota Senate |access-date=September 19, 2019}}</ref>

While in the Senate, Little was involved in efforts to address the rising cost of insulin. In December 2018, he convened an informal discussion at the state Capitol with patients, advocates, and lawmakers about insulin prices and said he had drafted several proposals aimed at controlling costs, including a price cap.<ref name="CBS-insulin">{{cite news |title=Minn. Lawmakers Discuss Reining In Soaring Insulin Costs |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/minn-lawmakers-open-discussions-on-high-insulin-costs/ |work=[[WCCO-TV|CBS Minnesota]] |date=December 12, 2018 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> By January 2019, MPR News described Little as a leading Senate advocate for several proposals intended to reduce insulin costs.<ref name="MPR-insulin-Jan">{{cite news |last=Bakst |first=Brian |title=State lawmakers hope to reverse insulin price spike |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2019/01/23/minn-lawmakers-hope-to-reverse-insulin-price-spike |work=[[Minnesota Public Radio|MPR News]] |date=January 23, 2019 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> An insulin-assistance provision passed both legislative chambers that spring but was omitted from the final health and human services budget agreement; Little subsequently convened bipartisan negotiations over an emergency assistance program.<ref name="MPR-insulin-May">{{cite news |last=Bierschbach |first=Briana |title=Despite solid votes for insulin help, it falls out of final budget deal |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2019/05/23/despite-solid-votes-for-insulin-help-it-falls-out-of-final-budget-deal |work=[[Minnesota Public Radio|MPR News]] |date=May 23, 2019 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="MPR-insulin-July">{{cite news |last=Bierschbach |first=Briana |title=Minnesota lawmakers say there's agreement on emergency insulin aid |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2019/07/29/minnesota-lawmakers-reach-deal-on-emergency-insulin-aid |work=[[Minnesota Public Radio|MPR News]] |date=July 29, 2019 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> The Legislature ultimately passed the [[Alec Smith Insulin Affordability Act]] in 2020.<ref name="House-insulin">{{cite web |title=Emergency insulin bill going to governor after House, Senate approve compromise |url=https://www.house.mn.gov/sessiondaily/Story/15226 |publisher=[[Minnesota House of Representatives]] |date=April 14, 2020 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

Little gained national attention in 2020 for his use of the [[social media]] app [[TikTok]]. By August, the ''Star Tribune'' reported that he had accumulated more than 130,000 followers, and ''Politico'' profiled him as one of a small number of elected officials making extensive use of the platform to reach younger voters.<ref name="PoliticoTikTok">{{cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2020/08/14/politicians-using-tiktok-matt-little-395620 |title=Meet The Politician Who Lives on TikTok |work=[[Politico]] |last=Cohen |first=Max |date=August 14, 2020 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="StribTikTok">{{cite news |last=Jackson |first=Zoë |title=Minnesota lawmaker scours TikTok for young voters |url=https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-lawmaker-scours-tiktok-for-young-voters/571998272 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune|Star Tribune]] |date=August 4, 2020 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

Little ran for reelection in 2020 but lost to Republican nominee [[Zach Duckworth]].<ref name="SOS2020">{{cite web |title=Results for State Senator District 58 |url=https://electionresults.sos.mn.gov/results/Index?ErsElectionId=136&scenario=StateSenate&DistrictId=546&show=Go |publisher=[[Minnesota Secretary of State]] |date=November 30, 2020 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Wilmes |first=Samuel |title=Duckworth defeats Little in battleground state Senate race |url=https://www.southernminn.com/northfield_news/news/article_f60fbf95-4124-5432-951c-bc9d2163ae48.html |access-date=November 9, 2020 |work=SouthernMinn.com |date=November 3, 2020}}</ref> The contest drew substantial outside spending from both parties. In late October, the ''Star Tribune'' reported that Republican groups had spent more than $300,000 to defeat Little and DFL-aligned groups had spent more than $400,000 to support him, describing him as a leading Republican target in the fight for control of the Senate.<ref name="Strib2020Spending">{{cite news |last1=Van Oot |first1=Torey |last2=Van Berkel |first2=Jessie |title=Tens of millions in campaign dollars flood fight for Minnesota Legislature |url=https://www.startribune.com/tens-of-millions-in-campaign-dollars-flood-fight-for-minnesota-legislature/572890951 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune|Star Tribune]] |date=October 27, 2020 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

In 2022, Little ran for Dakota County Attorney but lost to Kathy Keena, receiving 48.06% of the vote to Keena's 51.52%.<ref name="Dakota2022">{{cite web |title=Local Results in Dakota County |url=https://electionresults.sos.mn.gov/results/Index?CountyId=19&ErsElectionId=149&scenario=LocalRacesInCounty&show=Go |publisher=[[Minnesota Secretary of State]] |date=December 16, 2022 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="lrl" />

=== 2026 congressional candidacy ===
[[File:2026MattLittle.jpg|thumb|upright|Little campaigning in 2026]]
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Minnesota#District 2}}

On April 30, 2025, Little announced his candidacy for the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] in [[Minnesota's 2nd congressional district]], after incumbent [[Angie Craig]] decided to run for [[2026 United States Senate election in Minnesota|the state's open U.S. Senate seat]] instead. He was the first candidate to enter the Democratic primary.<ref name="Strib-launch" /> He was later joined by state representative [[Kaela Berg]] and state senator [[Matt Klein]], who became his principal rivals in the primary.<ref name="CBS-CD2">{{cite news |title=Race for Minnesota's 2nd Congressional District could prove to be highly competitive |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/minnesota-2nd-congressional-district-race-2026/ |work=[[WCCO-TV|CBS Minnesota]] |date=April 26, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Strib-primary">{{cite news |last=Kashiwagi |first=Sydney |title=Angie Craig's exit tests whether Minnesota's Second District is ready to move left |url=https://www.startribune.com/angie-craig-second-district-democratic-dfl-primary-little-berg-klein-august-11/601870082 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune]] |date=August 5, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

During [[Operation Metro Surge]], Little was among Democratic candidates who participated in protests against [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] activity in the southern Twin Cities suburbs.<ref name="Strib-ICE">{{cite news |last=Kashiwagi |first=Sydney |title=Operation Metro Surge puts immigration at the forefront in a crowded Minnesota congressional race |url=https://www.startribune.com/minnesota-immigration-second-congressional-district/601579292 |work=[[Minnesota Star Tribune]] |date=February 10, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> In April 2026, ''[[The Intercept]]'' reported that local [[Rapid response team (resistance movement)|rapid response]] units opposing ICE activity were concerned that Minnesota Democrats were co-opting the movement for votes, with some activists claiming that Little had used the movement for political gain.<ref name="Intercept-ICE">{{cite news |last1=Washington |first1=Jessica |last2=Frances |first2=C. |title=ICE Watchers Worry Democrats Are Trying to Co-Opt Their Movements For Votes |url=https://theintercept.com/2026/04/29/minnesota-congress-ice-democrats-matt-little/ |work=[[The Intercept]] |date=April 29, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

Little addressed the criticism during an interview with [[WCCO-TV]], saying that his involvement in the movement was personal because his wife, a [[naturalized citizen]] and a U.S. resident since age 10, had to carry documents during Operation Metro Surge. He said: "We posted some videos to hold them accountable, but there's a whole host of stuff we were doing that we don't post about, don't talk about. It was important to be out there for my family."<ref name="WCCO-May3">{{cite news |title=Matt Little says he'll drop out of race if he doesn't receive DFL endorsement |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/video/matt-little-says-hell-drop-out-of-race-if-he-doesnt-receive-dfl-endorsement/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |work=[[WCCO-TV|CBS Minnesota]] |date=May 3, 2026}}</ref> Later in the campaign, the ''Minnesota Star Tribune'' also reported that Little often discussed his wife's experience as an immigrant and her decision to keep her U.S. passport nearby during the federal immigration operation.<ref name="Strib-primary" />

Little said he would abide by the endorsement of the [[Minnesota Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party]] and support the endorsed candidate if he were not endorsed.<ref name="WCCO-May3" />

In a February 2026 precinct caucus straw poll, Little received 43.29% of the vote to Klein's 20.97% and Berg's 6.68%.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

On May 9, Little won the DFL endorsement at the Second Congressional District Endorsement Convention, receiving 63% of delegate votes on the first ballot, three percentage points above the threshold required for endorsement.<ref name="cd2-dflconvention" /><ref name="CBS-endorsement" /> Berg and Klein remained in the race.<ref name="cd2-dflconvention" /><ref name="Strib-primary" /> Although six DFL candidates appeared on the primary ballot, campaign coverage focused largely on Little, Klein, and Berg as the three leading contenders.<ref name= "Strib-primary" /><ref name= "APDecision">{{cite news |title= AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Minnesota's state primary |url= https://apnews.com/article/3625fa689d1535bec0f150bb0f006619 |work= [[Associated Press]] |date= August 10, 2026 |access-date= August 11, 2026}}</ref> The race was widely framed as a contest between the party's progressive and moderate wings, with Little and Berg running to Klein's left.<ref name= "Strib-primary" /><ref name= "Strib-spending">{{cite news |last= Kashiwagi |first= Sydney |title= Democratic divide fuels last-minute spending spree in Minnesota's Second District |url= https://www.startribune.com/mn-second-district-angie-craig-seat-us-house-klein-berg-little-tuesday-primary-pac-money-spending/601876065 |work= [[Minnesota Star Tribune]] |date= August 8, 2026 |access-date= August 11, 2026}}</ref> In the final weeks, outside groups spent millions of dollars in the race; the ''Star Tribune'' reported that [[314 Action]] had spent $2.5 million supporting Klein since July 20, while groups supporting Little had spent more than $407,000.<ref name= "Strib-spending" />

On August 11, Little won the primary and advanced to the general election against the Republican nominee, state senator [[Eric Pratt (politician)|Eric Pratt]].<ref name= "FOXPrimaryWin" />

== Political positions ==
[[File:MattLittle2026.jpg|thumb|Little speaking in 2026]]
=== Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) ===

During his 2026 congressional campaign, Little condemned [[Operation Metro Surge]] and called [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]] agents "lawless street gangs".<ref name="Little-ICE">{{cite web |title=Fighting to Get ICE OUT of Minnesota Now |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-to-get-ice-out-of-minnesota-now/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> He advocates replacing ICE with an agency that he says would operate in accordance with the [[Constitution of the United States|U.S. Constitution]], mandating clear identification for agents, restricting the [[qualified immunity]] of federal agents by amending [[Ku Klux Klan Act#Section 1 (42 USC § 1983)|Section 1983]] of [[Title 42 of the United States Code]], and ensuring transparency about the location of detainees.<ref name="Little-ICE" /> In February 2026, the ''Minnesota Star Tribune'' reported that Little supported getting rid of ICE provided it was replaced with an immigration-enforcement organization that could build public trust. MPR News later reported that Little and Berg had publicly called for the agency's abolition.<ref name="Strib-ICE" /><ref name="MPR-ICE">{{cite news |last=Kelley |first=Cait |title=After ICE surge, DFL leans into immigration as a campaign issue. Will it last? |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/04/23/after-ice-surge-dfl-leans-into-immigration-as-a-campaign-issue-will-it-last |work=[[Minnesota Public Radio|MPR News]] |date=April 23, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> His opposition to the federal immigration operation was also a prominent part of his campaigning in the southern Twin Cities suburbs during the winter of 2026.<ref name="Strib-ICE" />

=== Economy ===
Little has advocated a permanent expansion of the [[Child tax credit (United States)|U.S. Child Tax Credit]] and opposes [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs]].<ref name="Little-economy">{{cite web |title=Fighting for Lower Prices & An Economy that Works for Everyone |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-lower-prices-an-economy-that-works-for-everyone/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website= Matt Little for Congress}}</ref><ref name="KARE-primary">{{cite news |title=Three DFL primary candidates battle for U.S. House seat in Minnesota's 2nd Congressional District |url=https://www.kare11.com/article/news/local/breaking-the-news/three-dfl-primary-candidates-battle-for-us-house-seat-in-minnesotas-2nd-congressional-district/89-df956cf4-95d7-4ec6-950c-02646745bd76 |work=[[KARE (TV)|KARE 11]] |date=July 28, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref> He has also expressed support for organized labor and collective bargaining as part of his economic platform.<ref name="Little-economy" />

Little supports the Affordable Loans for Students Act, which would cap interest rates on current and future student loans at 2%.<ref name= "Little-studentloans">{{cite web |title= Fighting for Fair Student Loans |url= https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-fair-student-loans/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> His platform also calls for restoring loan balances to their original principal amounts, strengthening loan-servicer accountability and forgiving remaining federal student-loan balances after 20 years.<ref name="Little-studentloans" />

=== Health care ===
Little supports [[Medicare for All]]. During his 2026 congressional campaign, he argued that Medicare should be made available to all Americans rather than relying on further incremental changes to the existing health insurance system.<ref name="Little-healthcare">{{cite web |title=Fighting for Medicare for All |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-healthcare/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> The ''Minnesota Star Tribune'' described Medicare for All as one of the pillars of his campaign, and FOX 9 likewise identified the proposal as a central part of his platform.<ref name="Strib-primary" /><ref name="FOXPrimaryWin" />

Little has also advocated expanding the ability of [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] and [[Medicaid]] to negotiate prescription drug prices.<ref name="Little-healthcare" /> His congressional health-care platform cites his work on insulin affordability in the Minnesota Senate.<ref name="Little-healthcare" /><ref name= "CBS-insulin" /><ref name="MPR-insulin-Jan" />

In March 2026, [[National Nurses United]] endorsed Little's campaign, citing his support for a health-care system providing universal coverage and identifying Medicare for All as the model it favored.<ref name= "NNU">{{cite web |title= National Nurses United endorses Matt Little for Minnesota's 2nd District |url= https://www.nationalnursesunited.org/press/national-nurses-united-endorses-matt-little-for-minnesotas-2nd-district |publisher=[[National Nurses United]] |date=March 26, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

=== Israel–Palestine conflict ===
Little condemned [[Hamas]]'s [[October 7 attacks]], as well as [[Israel]]'s subsequent military response, which he has called "[[Gaza genocide|genocidal]]".<ref name="Little-Israel">{{cite web |title=Fighting for a Just & Lasting Peace in Israel & Palestine |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-a-just-lasting-peace-in-israel-palestine/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref><ref name="MPR-Israel">{{cite news |last=Cox |first=Peter |title=Amid Middle East conflict, Minnesota Democrats more vocally criticize Israel's actions |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/06/18/amid-middle-east-conflict-minnesota-democrats-more-vocally-criticize-israels-actions |work=[[Minnesota Public Radio|MPR News]] |date=June 18, 2026 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="FOXPrimaryWin" /> He has advocated ending [[Israel–United States military relations|U.S. military aid and weapons sales to Israel]], permitting humanitarian aid to enter Gaza, removing [[Israeli settlement|illegal Israeli settlements from Palestinian territories]], and establishing a [[two-state solution]] for Israel and Palestine.<ref name= "Little-Israel" /><ref name="FOXPrimaryWin" /> His call for an arms embargo became one of the distinctions between him and Klein during the closing days of the Democratic primary.<ref name="Strib-spending" />

=== LGBTQ rights ===
Little has advocated passage of the [[Equality Act (United States)|Equality Act]], which would prohibit discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity, and sex; protecting ''[[Obergefell v. Hodges]]''; and banning [[Conversion therapy in the United States|conversion therapy]] nationally.<ref name= "Little-LGBTQ">{{cite web |title=Fighting for LGBTQIA2S+ Rights |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-fot-lgbtqia2s-rights/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> During his speech to the May 2026 DFL endorsing convention, he identified [[transgender]] rights as one of the issues on which he wanted the party to take a more assertive position.<ref name= "cd2-dflconvention" />

Little opposes the Trump administration's restrictions on transgender people serving in the military. His campaign has called for reversing the policy whose enforcement the Supreme Court permitted while litigation continued in ''United States v. Shilling''.<ref name="Little-LGBTQ" /><ref name="AP-Shilling">{{cite news |last=Sherman |first=Mark |title=Supreme Court allows Trump ban on transgender members of the military to take effect, for now |url=https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-transgender-military-ban-ef67038857bd5b99e128bf0b8866afb4 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=May 6, 2025 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref><ref name="SCOTUS-Shilling">{{cite web |title=Miscellaneous Order, May 6, 2025 |url=https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/courtorders/050625zr_6j37.pdf |publisher=[[Supreme Court of the United States]] |date=May 6, 2025 |access-date=August 11, 2026}}</ref>

=== Anti-corruption ===
Little has publicly refused campaign funding from [[AIPAC]], [[Super PAC|super PACs]], health insurance PACs, and corporate PACs.<ref name="Little-corruption">{{cite web |title=Fighting for Anti-Corruption Policies |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-anti-corruption-policies/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> A ban on corporate campaign contributions was one of the campaign positions highlighted in the ''Minnesota Star Tribune''{{'}}s coverage of the primary.<ref name= "Strib-primary" /> Little supports overturning ''[[Citizens United v. FEC]]'' and ''[[Buckley v. Valeo]]'' to permit campaign spending limits, banning members of Congress from trading stocks, requiring presidents and close family members to divest business assets and place their value in a [[blind trust]], and creating a pardon board for [[Federal pardons in the United States|federal pardons]].<ref name="Little-corruption" />

Little also calls for preventing [[Lobbying|lobbyists]] and corporations from fundraising for federal political campaigns or donating money to government events and functions, greater disclosure of corporate and PAC campaign contributions, and a publicly financed federal campaign system.<ref name="Little-corruption" />

=== Federal taxes ===
Little wants to raise the [[Corporate tax in the United States|federal corporate tax rate]], increase taxes on high-income earners, and eliminate the [[carried interest]] loophole.<ref name="Little-taxes">{{cite web |title=Fighting for Tax Cuts |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-tax-cuts/ |access-date= August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> During the 2026 campaign, he called for a wealth tax; the ''Minnesota Star Tribune'' reported that he promoted the proposal in his speech to the DFL endorsing convention, while FOX 9 described taxes on the wealthy as part of his general-election platform.<ref name= "cd2-dflconvention" /><ref name="FOXPrimaryWin" /> Little also supports raising the income cap subject to [[Social Security (United States)|Social Security]] taxation to strengthen the program's finances.<ref name="Little-SS">{{cite web |title=Fighting for Social Security |url=https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-social-security/ |access-date=August 11, 2026 |website=Matt Little for Congress}}</ref>

=== Public safety and police ===
Little opposes reducing police staffing and has expressed concern about [[cybercrime]], fentanyl trafficking, and human trafficking. He supports funding law-enforcement training and the [[Dakota County, Minnesota|Dakota County]] Safety and Mental Health Alternative Response Training Center, commonly known as the SMART Center.<ref name= "Little-safety">{{cite web |title= Fighting for Safe Neighborhoods |url= https://littleforcongress.com/key-issues/fighting-for-safe-neighborhoods/ |access-date= August 11, 2026 |website= Matt Little for Congress}}</ref> He has also argued that law-enforcement officers who use unnecessary force or violate due process should be held accountable.<ref name= "Little-safety" />
